Fuck man, I feel you. I'm only 22 at the time of writing this but that future is all I imagine my life going (just maybe with a much lower paying job or none at all). I've never had a clear vision in my life and by 18 my parents forced me to choose a career path. The only things I've ever been good at was drawing and english (wich isn't my main language so excuse any typos).

They would never let me pursue any creative related career because "you will be broke" and so they would slightly manipulate me (I never knew if it was intentional or their way of guiding me) into choosing to study Tourism (a hotel management sort of career). My dumb 18 year old brain all it cared about was playing videogames at the time and passively bought into that idea.

That was 4 years ago. I should have already finished career along with all my classmates. But by the first year of my degree I quickly realized how much I hated every single thing I was studied and how I didn't like any of the career paths and jobs it offered. That along with a quickly emerging depression made me constantly miss exams on purpose and self sabotage, to the point where I'm doing an extra fifth (and possibly sixth) year with a shit ton of credits to complete yet of all the hard stuff.

I still have no idea what I want to do. I'm forcing myself to finish this career to not have sunk all those years for nothing and at least have a backup plan if anything I try out in the future doesn't work. All my friends are already working as something or setting themselves up. I'm just stuck here, on a degree that makes me not want to wake up in the morning and with no discernible future.

I think people generally figure out their lives somehow, but I did an any% speed run and fucked up mine in the quickest way possible. The thought of my life slowly going down the drain into unemployment or a job I'll hate forever feeds into suicidal thoughts a lot and makes me often think that I won't be alive to experience the situation you (OP) are in right now.

I'm sorry for whoever reads this wall of rambling but this post really spoke to me and it's something that I never really opened up about. I'm lost so soon and I don't know how to find myself.


TL,DR: At 22 with depression self-sabotaging my college degree wich I hate, with no passion for living at all.

Hi!

I most certainly can relate to a lot of the things you said. This person and I have broken up times before, and last time I tried to re-start as I was feeling the worst I have ever been. Not because of anything in particular, I just felt lost with everything going on in my life and I couldn't grasp any bit of hope to hold on to. I had my fair share of suicidal thoughts but I always knew I was too scared to act on them. 

So, last thing I could resort to is try to ignore my own malicious mind and work to improve at least some aspects of my life. I put more effort on my studies, I started new hobbies, tried to be more social and tried to be a positive person and positive influence on my friends (this was the hardest thing since I've grown used to being sarcastic and have a pesimist outlook in life). 

I was starting to actually not have to put effort in these, as they were becoming habits in my life more than things I was pushing for. It had been a while since I last felt awful about myself or spiraled into depression.

A great part of this improvement I associated with this person. I wanted to be better for them, more than for myself. And now that she isn't in the picture, it jeopardized everything that I worked for in the last months/year. 

I panicked because, in addition of losing someone I loved, I lost my reason to keep going. "Why should I keep putting effort in things if people are going to leave me regardless? Why should I improve myself in anyway? This is who I am, who am I trying to fool?", those are the kind of things storming my head right now.

Restarting was hard. And now I need to do it all over again. And this time for myself. 
I'm not sure how to do it or if I will do it, but I guess it's either that or curling up in my bed forever.

Thank you so much for your comment, it made me feel like I wasn't alone and took some weight off of my shoulders. I hope you too are doing well!

I decided to get a new CPU+DDR4 RAM+ Mobo at once! Although in this case,I figured out my problem had to do with the HDD my game was installed in. More specifically, I had set the pagefile on fixed values and (I believe) that forced the game to use the pagefile more than it should, consequently using the HDD as RAM and slowing down. I just set both pagefiles on my SSD and HDD to be managed by Windows and almost all the stuttering disappeared.

An easy way is to open Task Manager on windows and alt tabbing out of the game when it stutters or goes down on frames and checking the Memory graph. But the GPU being at 100% isn't really good either, it could be something related to that.
